_note: ModBus is one of the oldest and most widely used industrial protocols in the world. It's simple: a client asks a server to read or write numbered registers and coils, and the server answers. It's also completely unauthenticated - there's no password, no signature, and no encryption in the base protocol. In this lesson you'll learn to read ModBus traffic and understand what it's saying.

Using the ModBus table, you'll decode requests and responses captured from the lab network: which function code was used, which registers were read, and what values came back. You'll learn to map raw register numbers onto real-world meanings like temperature or rudder angle. The table is read-only in this lesson; changing values comes later, once you understand exactly what you'd be changing.

- Name the common ModBus function codes (read coils, read holding registers, write single register, and so on).
- Decode a ModBus request and response pair from the Packet Console.
- Use the ModBus table to follow a register's value over time.
- Map register addresses onto the physical quantities they represent.
- Explain why ModBus's lack of authentication is a security problem.
